scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: An IT Department user (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) reports they
cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) -- inter-department routing
between IT and CS seems broken. They suspect router0 (which connects both
segments) dropped one of its department interfaces or a static/RIP entry. Please
confirm the inter-department fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Inter-department L3 forwarding between the IT subnet (192.168.1.0/24) and the CS subnet (192.168.2.0/24) is operating normally. On router0, both department interfaces are up with correct addressing (eth0=192.168.1.1/24, eth1=192.168.2.1/24) and have link detected. The routing table shows connected routes for both networks: “C>* 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, eth0” and “C>* 192.168.2.0/24 is directly connected, eth1.” RIP is enabled but not required for this local inter-VLAN routing path.

End-to-end tests confirm reachability in both directions: from it_hod (192.168.1.2) to cs_hod (192.168.2.2) and cs_lab1 (192.168.2.3) return 0% loss with ~1–1.7 ms RTT; reverse ping from cs_hod to it_hod also succeeds. Host default gateways are correctly set (it_hod via 192.168.1.1; CS hosts via 192.168.2.1).

Mechanism: Because both subnets are directly connected to router0, inter-department traffic is switched to L3 locally on router0 without relying on dynamic routes. If an interface were down or a gateway misconfigured, these tests would have failed; they did not.

Localization: No faults observed on router0 eth0/eth1, nor on the tested hosts.

Root cause: No network fault was present at the time of testing; the reported outage could not be reproduced.

Corrective fix: None required. If the issue recurs, capture ping/arp outputs from the affected host during the event to check for transient ARP/host-stack issues.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0's IT and CS interfaces are up and inter-department routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states router0's eth0/eth1 are up with correct addresses and link detected, and confirms inter-department routing and end-to-end reachability at baseline.

The agent's logs show interface IPs up on router0 and hosts and successful bidirectional pings between IT and CS hosts; its conclusion (no anomaly) follows directly from these observations. Minor omission: the routing-table snippet was truncated, but interface bindings plus successful pings adequately ground the diagnosis.
